discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion: ground-state cooling and quantum coupling of mechanical oscillators

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

motivation: Following the 2025 recognition of macroscopic quantum effects in electrical circuits, the natural next frontier is quantum mechanics of massive mechanical objects. In 2010 Cleland and co-workers coupled a superconducting qubit to a micromechanical resonator, bringing a visible mechanical object into its quantum ground state and controlling single phonons. Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg independently established cavity optomechanics, using radiation pressure to cool mechanical oscillators to the ground state, observe quantum back-action and ponderomotive squeezing, and create entanglement between light and motion. Together they turned a century-old question - does quantum mechanics apply to tangible objects? - into a controllable laboratory platform. Their work underpins quantum-limited force and displacement sensing, microwave-optical transduction for networking superconducting quantum processors, and tests of decoherence and gravity in the quantum regime. It is a decisive, mature achievement in macroscopic quantum physics.
